title: Design System: CEEDO Collections — Back Office

primary.purpose: The office acting: primary button, focus ring, caret, focused control border, check indicator, facet chip, office mark.

chassis-900.purpose: The chassis itself: rail, dialog head, scrim, tooltip, checked checkbox.

chassis-accent.purpose: The machine's only warm metal. Brand tile, user initials chip, chassis focus ring. Three uses, no more; never an action.

chassis-dim.purpose: Resting nav text, about 12.9:1 on chassis-900. The contrast floor on the machine.

chassis-ink.purpose: Current nav item, dialog head text.

ribbon.purpose: Shortage, void, overdue, and the destructive act.

amber.purpose: True but not yet a failure: a closed shift not yet synced, an overage.

proof.purpose: Agreement. A balanced shift, a successful notice.

tape.purpose: The page ground and every recessed band.

tape-raised.purpose: The raised surface: table body, panels, dialog body, popovers, listbox.

tape-sunk.purpose: The blank a clerk writes in. Every input, select and checkbox.

ink.purpose: Every figure and every primary word.

ink-2.purpose: Standing notes, captions, secondary labels. About 9:1 on the field.

ink-3.purpose: Placeholders, muted rows, the em-dash zero. About 5.6:1 — the text floor on the field.

rule-strong.purpose: Control borders and the table head's lower edge.

display.purpose: The screen heading in the header band (1.5rem/700/-0.025em), and the sign-in name on the chassis.

headline.purpose: The /no-access refusal, on the chassis. One place.

title.purpose: Panel heads and dialog titles — a block's name, not a page's.

body.purpose: Table cells, control text, dialog copy, nav items. Standing notes cap at 68ch.

body-small.purpose: Pager counts, help text, secondary cell detail, quiet marks.

label.purpose: The .caption utility: every field label, column head and totals label. Letterspaced small caps at 0.08em.

rail-label.purpose: The chassis's own small caps at 0.12em: group headings at 40% dim, wordmark subtitle and staff role at 50%.

measure.purpose: IBM Plex Mono for serials, lease ids, credential ids, PINs and secrets. Never for emphasis or headings.

shadows.name: docket
shadows.purpose: The dialog, lifted off the field onto the chassis.

motion.name: ease-exponential
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for the docket and the mobile rail.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Colour transitions on controls, buttons, rail items.

motion.name: docket-in
motion.value: @keyframes docket-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, calc(-50% + 10px)) scale(0.985) } } — 180ms

motion.name: retally
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the totals row re-tallying when the filter changes. Never fires on mount.

layout.rail: 16rem (w-64) sticky navy chassis, no right border; 56px header; 32px nav rows; below lg a 56px sticky bar plus an 18rem drawer.
layout.content: px-4 py-6, sm:px-6, lg:px-8 lg:py-7, inside a centred max-w-[96rem].
layout.header: 1.5rem/700 heading, muted note at max 68ch in ink-3, right-aligned actions, mb-6, no divider rule.
layout.tape: One rounded-xl hairline-framed white block: filter slip, table head, rows, the close, proof line, pager.
layout.rhythm: 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 24px. Cells px-3 py-1.5; fields stack at 14px; panels px-4 py-3.5 over px-4 py-2.5.

components.name: Teaching Empty State
components.description: A required per-screen sentence saying what the record IS and what depends on it, with the control that resolves it.
components.html: No sections yet. A section divides a market into its trades — Fish, Meat, Vegetable, Dry goods — and sets the billing period its stalls inherit. A market facility has to exist before a section can belong to one.

narrative.overview:
The world is the treasury cash-proof ritual: a dark chassis holding a pale continuous field of figures. Every screen is a proof — a column of entries, a hairline rule, a total, and one line that says whether it agrees. The rail is dark because it is the machine; the field is pale because it is read all day at an office desk. This is not a light/dark theme. There is one theme, no prefers-color-scheme block and no switcher, both user-confirmed in PRODUCT.md.

The material is CEEDO's sibling app, berlcamp/hris: a navy sidebar on an off-white page, white panels, a hairline #d9dfe5 rule, navy for the office acting, brass spent twice, and a multiplicative corner ramp instead of a single rectilinear step. The warm carbon-and-paper palette this world was first built in was translated into that one, on the user's instruction, so the two apps read as the same office. Topology, control vocabulary, state vocabulary, the colour-reserve discipline, motion and the running proof are unchanged; only the tones and the corners moved.

The surface is built for an accounting clerk at an office desktop all day, so density and scanning speed outrank expression. Composition is still made of rules. Colour is the scarce resource — it lives at edges, in row-gutter bars, in state marks and on the variance line, and never as a fill behind a figure. The confirmed anti-reference is skeuomorphic pastiche; the collector tablet app is explicitly not a visual reference for this surface.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds, one theme: navy chassis for the machine, off-white field for the figures.
Rules and hairline frames, not shadows. No resting surface carries a shadow.
One multiplicative radius ramp (0.3rem to 1.3rem), applied by role, not by whim.
Achromatic figures. Colour only at edges, gutter marks, state marks and the variance line.
Every state legible with colour removed — strike-through, ink bars, weight, half-density.
One type family; mono reserved for measurement.
Brass appears exactly twice on the chassis and nowhere else.
Motion is state, never decoration, and never on page load.
An empty screen teaches: it says what a record here is and what depends on it.

rules.name: The Achromatic Figure Rule
rules.body: Colour never fills the ground behind a number. A peso amount is ink or muted ink, never tinted by its row's status. Colour appears at edges, in the row gutter, inside a state mark, and on the variance line — nowhere else.

rules.name: The Colour-Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: No state is signalled by colour alone. Voided is struck through; a row needing attention carries a solid ink bar in its gutter; the current rail item is set in medium weight on the same ground its hover uses; disabled is half-density. The mark always contains its own word.

rules.name: The Ink Floor Rule
rules.body: ink-3 (#5c646f, about 5.6:1) is the lightest text permitted on the field. Nothing lighter is text. On the chassis, chassis-dim (#d9dfe5, about 12.9:1) is the floor.

rules.name: The Brass-Is-Ornament Rule
rules.body: Brass marks the machine's identity — brand tile, user chip, chassis focus ring — and never carries an action. A brass button does not exist here.

rules.name: The No Ad-Hoc Grey Rule
rules.body: The palette is locked. A grey that is not in the token set does not exist; reach for a rule, a field step or an ink step.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Sans carries headings, labels, controls and data. There is no display face and no second sans.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Measurement Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for things that are counted, matched or transcribed character-by-character — serials, ids, PINs, secrets. Money is not mono: it is Plex Sans with tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Product UI at a consistent desk DPI. Fixed rem steps only; no fluid clamp() anywhere.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set at base on every table and every [data-figures] block, so figures line up on the decimal everywhere rather than only where someone remembered.

rules.name: The Fixed Frame Rule
rules.body: Rail, header band, filter slip, tape, proof and pager hold their places across every route. Only the tape's contents change.

rules.name: The Density Rule
rules.body: Comfortable spacing that halves the visible rows is a cost paid by the person who uses this surface most. Row padding does not grow.

rules.name: The Value-Step Rule
rules.body: The rail needs no border. Where two grounds differ enough in value, the step is the edge; adding a rule there only thickens the machine.

rules.name: The Frame-Not-Float Rule
rules.body: A block is defined by a 1px rule, a radius and a ground step. If a surface needs separating, frame it; do not float it.

rules.name: The Overlay-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means 'portalled above the page'. Anything that lives in the flow gets none, and never as a hard offset.

rules.name: The Role-Not-Whim Rule
rules.body: A radius is chosen by what the element is, not by how it looks in isolation: control -> lg, framed block -> xl, state mark -> 4xl. A sixth radius on a seventh kind of element is drift.

rules.name: The Accountant's Close
rules.body: A total is closed by a hairline above and a double rule below (.rule-close). It is painted as two background gradients rather than border-bottom: double, because under border-collapse: collapse a double border resolves its corners against the neighbouring cell and drops a vertical hairline at every column boundary. Never re-implement the close as a double border inside a collapsed table.

rules.name: The No-Entrance Rule
rules.body: Nothing choreographs a page load. The clerk is mid-task, not watching an entrance.

rules.name: The One Authored Moment Rule
rules.body: retally is the only place in the app where motion draws the eye on purpose. Everything else is a state change arriving.

dos: Do treat the chassis/field split as two materials in one scene: navy is the machine (rail, dialog head, scrim, tooltip, checkbox fill), off-white is the paper the figures are read off.
Do close every summed column with .rule-close — hairline above, double rule below.
Do keep the figure field achromatic; spend colour on edges, gutter bars, state marks and the variance line.
Do give every state a non-colour carrier: strike-through, an ink bar, weight, a word inside the mark, half-density.
Do pick a radius by role — lg for controls, xl for framed blocks, 4xl for marks, md for nav rows and focus rings, sm for the checkbox.
Do keep primary actions navy and brass ornamental: brand tile, user chip, chassis focus ring, and nothing else.
Do set every field label, column head and totals label in the .caption small caps, and every chassis label at 0.12em.
Do reserve IBM Plex Mono for serials, ids, PINs and secrets; money stays Plex Sans with tabular figures.
Do write an empty that says what the record is and what depends on it, and pass an emptyAction whenever a control can resolve it.
Do build blocks from Panel, Notice, Mark and DataTable rather than new one-off shapes.

Do keep every screen keyboard-complete: the global / focuses the filter, Radix handles focus trapping and restore, dialogs land on the first real field, sortable heads are buttons carrying aria-sort, and icon-only controls carry aria-label.
Do declare sortValue / searchValue / total / facet explicitly on a column instead of parsing what render produced.
Do keep ink-3 as the lightest text on the field and chassis-dim as the lightest on the chassis.
donts: Don't add a theme switcher, a prefers-color-scheme block or a dark variant of the field. One theme, user-confirmed.
Don't put a shadow on anything that lives in the flow. Shadows belong to portalled overlays only, and never as a hard offset.
Don't fill a ground behind a number with colour, or tint a peso amount by its row's status.
Don't signal anything with colour alone.
Don't put brass on a button, a link or any other action.
Don't add a right border to the rail, or a divider rule under the screen heading — the value step and the gap are the separation.
Don't implement the accountant's close as border-bottom: double inside a border-collapse: collapse table — it drops vertical seams at every column boundary.
Don't put a kicker, eyebrow or overline above a screen heading.
Don't introduce a grey, a radius step or a type size that is not in the token set, and don't use fluid clamp() sizing.
Don't ship a table or a resource without empty copy, and don't let 'Nothing here yet.' stand in for it.
Don't choreograph a page load, or animate anything from an invisible default.
Don't add a second type family, or use mono for emphasis, headings or 'code' styling.
Don't add texture, torn edges, rules that pretend to be perforations, or any other skeuomorphic paper effect.
Don't let a denied read and an empty table look the same.
openDecisions: The sibling app runs DM Sans; this app deliberately kept IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono, because the tabular figures are load-bearing here. The family is an open decision for the user, not drift.
Date inputs use the native type="date" control: it submits ISO, and its display order is the OS locale's. An open question for the user rather than a defect.
knownResiduals: A sub-pixel seam of about 2/255 at column boundaries in the totals row — a border-collapse compositing artifact, measured and judged imperceptible. Not repaired, not canonized.
formatCell in components/admin/resource-table.tsx still prints raw numbers for rates.amount and surcharge_bps — pre-existing, and a data decision rather than a design one.
